terms.definition: The role of a species in its ecosystem: how it uses resources and interacts with other species.
terms.examiner: Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche in the same habitat for long.

terms.definition: The largest population of a species that a habitat can support indefinitely.
terms.examiner: Set by limiting factors such as food, space and predation.

terms.definition: A factor whose effect on a population grows as the population density rises, such as disease, food supply or predation.
terms.examiner: Density-independent factors, such as drought or fire, act regardless of density.

terms.definition: Species that reproduce quickly, with many offspring and little parental care.
terms.examiner: They recover quickly from exploitation; K-selected species do not.

terms.definition: Species that reproduce slowly, with few offspring, long lives and much parental care.
terms.examiner: They are easily over-exploited and slow to recover.

terms.definition: The first species to colonise bare ground or water at the start of succession.
terms.examiner: They tolerate harsh conditions and change them, for example by adding organic matter.

terms.definition: The largest harvest that can be taken from a population year after year without reducing it.
terms.examiner: It is hard to estimate, so harvests set at it often lead to over-exploitation.
